audit_event.notes: Per design.md §9.6, every successful REVOKE is recorded as a five-tuple in audit-log; error_code is null because the path is the success path. Trigger: iFay reports task completion (DISCLOSURE → HP confirmation).

irreversibility_note: Per Requirement 4.3 the Mandate's status is now terminal-Revoked; any subsequent RP call referencing this mandate_id MUST fail with 1006 E_REVOKED. The only recovery path is a fresh BOOTSTRAP that issues a new Mandate with a different mandate_id.
notes: Validates that `RevokeReason = 'task-completed'` produces a well-formed REVOKE → REVOKE_RECEIPT round-trip. Trigger: iFay reports task completion (DISCLOSURE → HP confirmation). Requirement 9.4 categorises this reason as a decoupling-state recognition trigger; the receipt lists exactly the directly-revoked Mandate (no children in this vector — see `cascade-depth-2` for the cascade case).

signature_verification.note: REVOKE envelope is signed by HP (Requirement 4.1.3 — REVOKE auth-strength ≥ BOOTSTRAP auth-strength). REVOKE_RECEIPT / ERROR is signed by MS. Both envelopes use canonical CBOR as signing input regardless of wire encoding.

summary: REVOKE with reason='task-completed': iFay-initiated decoupling per Requirement 4.1.4-5. The iFay's report is treated as a Disclosure_Report and HP confirms via REVOKE; the iFay never revokes its own Mandate.
trigger: iFay reports task completion (DISCLOSURE → HP confirmation)
